title: Lemonade Change
prompt: At a lemonade stand, each lemonade costs `$5`. Customers are standing in a queue, given as an array `bills`, where `bills[i]` is the bill the `i`-th customer pays with ($5, $10, or $20). You must provide the correct change for each customer so that the net transaction is that the customer pays $5. You start with no change on hand. Return `true` if you can provide every customer correct change, or `false` otherwise.

examples.explanation: You can provide change for each customer: from the two $5 bills and one $10 bill collected, you can give $15 change to the customer paying with $20 as one $10 and one $5.
After the first two $5s and two $10s, you have no $5 bills left to give as change for the $20, since $15 change can't be made from two $10 bills alone.
The very first customer pays with a $10, but you start with no bills on hand, so no $5 change can be given.

hints: You only ever need to track how many $5 and $10 bills you're holding — $20 bills are never given back as change.
For a $10 payment, change is forced (one $5). For a $20 payment, there are two ways to make $15 change — which one should you prefer?

Always prefer giving a $10 + $5 combo for $20 payments over three $5 bills, since $5 bills are more flexible and can cover either kind of future change. Greedily using the least flexible bills first is optimal.

solution.approach: Track only counts of $5 and $10 bills on hand, since $20 bills are never used as change. When a $10 arrives, the only valid change is a single $5. When a $20 arrives, prefer paying with a $10 and a $5 over three $5 bills whenever possible, because $5 bills are the only bill that can make change for a $10, so hoarding them is strictly better. If at any point the required change can't be made, return false.
